newsitem.title: COTE D'IVOIRE: Ivorian coffee bean exports rise in February.
newsitem.headline: Ivorian coffee bean exports rise in February.

text.p: Ivory Coast exported 13,527 tonnes of robusta coffee beans in February, against 5,373 tonnes in January and 13,536 tonnes in February 1996, official shipping data showed.
Cumulative exports in the first five months of the 1996/97 (October-September) season were 31,727 tonnes against 37,764 tonnes in the same period of 1995/96.
Ivorian coffee marketing started later in 1996/97 following low world prices in late 1996, tighter bank lending policies to exporters and quality problems slowing grading.
The season also opened later, in mid-November rather than early October.
The data showed 11,924 tonnes of February 1996 exports went from Abidjan, the main port, with 1,603 tonnes shipped from Ivory Coast's second port, San Pedro.
Coffee product exports, from Abidjan, included 660 tonnes of soluble coffee and six tonnes of roasted coffee.
Ivory Coast has forecast a 1996/97 coffee crop of 230,000 tonnes, against 180,000 tonnes recorded last year.
